audit.whatIsWrong: Nowhere in either layer is it stated that Spirit Cleave's cooldown and cast time scale with Yone's attack speed — which makes Wither a direct cooldown-extension tool, not merely a slow.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Spirit Cleave's cooldown and cast time scale with attack speed." Wither's headline effect is an attack-speed slow. Against Yone that means Nasus's W does something it does against almost nobody else: it physically lengthens the cooldown on his shield-and-damage button and slows the cast animation. This is the single most valuable interaction in the matchup and the strongest mechanical argument for Wither being worth a point early, and it is entirely absent.
audit.corrected: Spirit Cleave's cooldown and cast time both scale with attack speed, so Withering Yone stretches his shield cooldown and slows the cast — the slow is doing double work.
sources: champ-data/_kits/nasus.json — W "decelerating their Move Speed and Attack Speed"

audit.whatIsWrong: "slow him mid-animation so the spirit-cleave whiffs" and "Wither him mid-dash so his spirit-cleave whiffs" describe Wither as interrupting a dash and causing a cone ability to miss.
audit.why: Wither is a decaying slow on move speed and attack speed. It does not interrupt a dash in flight, and it cannot make Spirit Cleave whiff — Spirit Cleave is a cone centred on Yone, so a slow on Yone does not move the cone off Nasus. The advice happens to point at the right button for the wrong reason, which matters because the real effect (extending the cooldown, per the point above) is far better and gets lost.
audit.corrected: Wither does not interrupt the dash or make the cone miss. What it does is lengthen Spirit Cleave's cooldown and cast time, because both scale with attack speed.

audit.whatIsWrong: The recommended build is armour-heavy (Plated Steelcaps, Frozen Heart) with no note that half of Yone's auto-attack damage is magic.
audit.why: Way of the Hunter: "Yone deals magic damage with every second Attack." Yone is hybrid by default before any item choice, so armour answers only every other auto. A Nasus who stacks armour into a scaling crit Yone and cannot understand why he is still losing the extended fight is running into exactly this. The late-game section attributes his takeover purely to crit and mobility and never mentions the damage split.
audit.corrected: Way of the Hunter makes every second attack magic damage — armour alone answers half his autos, so magic resist has to enter the build against a scaling Yone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spirit Cleave's shield is mentioned as generic poke with no note that its value scales with the number of champions hit.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Grants a shield to Yone, the value is increased by the number of champions hit by the swipe." In a 1v1 lane that is one champion, so his shield is at its structural minimum in exactly the isolated duel Nasus wants — and correspondingly larger in the teamfights Nasus should avoid. That is a concrete reason to take the fight in the side lane rather than grouped, which is the plan the late-game text already recommends without giving the mechanical reason.
audit.corrected: Spirit Cleave's shield scales with champions hit, so it is at its weakest in the 1v1 and strongest in a teamfight.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names only Soul Unbound and carries no number; the packet counts 2 sequencing cues but no concrete timing anywhere.
audit.why: Soul Unbound is 22/19/16/13/10 — a 22 second window at rank 1 that shrinks to 10 by rank 5, which is a much sharper drop than most abilities and changes how punishable he is as the lane goes on. Spirit Cleave is 14s base before attack-speed scaling. Fate Sealed is 120/100/80.
audit.corrected: Soul Unbound 22s at rank 1 falling to 10s at rank 5. Spirit Cleave 14s base. Fate Sealed 120s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer's "He snaps back when it ends. Wither him there." for Soul Unbound.
audit.why: This is right and worth keeping. Soul Unbound returns Yone's spirit to the body he left behind, so the return point is fixed and known in advance — standing on the body is genuinely the play. I only added the cooldown number rather than changing the read.

edits.after: Spirit Cleave shields him least in a 1v1 — its value scales with champions hit, and that is only you.

edits.after: Wither stretches Spirit Cleave's cooldown, which scales with his attack speed, but with no ult neither of you can commit a kill.

edits.before: Yone is genuinely even with you at levels 1-3, which for you means you concede nothing but also can't punish — he pokes with Q1/Q2 and the W spirit-cleave, and if you walk up to throw a raw Q he just dances back. Don't trade for the sake of it: last-hit with Siphoning Strike, soak the poke on Soul Eater lifesteal, and start hoarding stacks. The one moment to wake up is his level 3 Q3 dash — if he commits the third Q for the knockup, Wither him mid-dash so his spirit-cleave whiffs and his E-rewind can't pull him out clean.
edits.after: Yone is genuinely even with you at levels 1-3, which for you means you concede nothing but also can't punish — he pokes with Mortal Steel and Spirit Cleave, and if you walk up to throw a raw Q he just dances back. Don't trade for the sake of it: last-hit with Siphoning Strike, soak the poke on Soul Eater lifesteal, and start hoarding stacks. The moment to wake up is the third Mortal Steel, the one that dashes and knocks up — Wither the instant he lands, because Spirit Cleave's cooldown scales with his attack speed.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 tilt slightly his way — he out-pokes you and his mobility means your raw Q never connects on a moving target, so play for farm and don't chase. Level 6 is your window: Fury of the Sands plus Wither is the one all-in he can't kite. Ult for the bonus HP and the AoE burn, slow his attack speed and movement to nothing so the Q3 knockup is your only thing to dodge, and grind him out with lifesteal while he can't reposition. Bait the E spirit-rewind first if you can — once it's down he has no second escape.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 tilt slightly his way — he out-pokes you and your raw Q never connects on a moving target, so play for farm and don't chase. Level 6 is your window: Fury of the Sands plus Wither is the one all-in he can't kite. The attack-speed cut is doing double work here, because Spirit Cleave's cooldown and cast time both scale with attack speed, so Withering him stretches his shield. Bait Soul Unbound first — 22s at rank 1, and once it is down he has no second escape.

edits.before: This is where Yone reclaims it. Once he has crit and his combo is online, his Q3 knockup into R lets him pick the skirmish, and his mobility means he engages and disengages on his terms while your stacked Q struggles to land on something that's never standing still. Your Wither is still your best tool — it's the only thing that pins him for a full duel — but in an extended fight a fed Yone out-DPSes your lifesteal. Play for splitpush pressure where your stacks shine in a clean 1v1, and let your team body-block his R so he can't kite you forever.
edits.after: This is where Yone reclaims it. Once he has crit and his combo is online, the third Mortal Steel into Fate Sealed lets him pick the skirmish, and your stacked Q struggles to land on something never standing still. Note that Way of the Hunter makes every second attack magic damage, so armour alone answers half his autos and magic resist has to enter the build. Wither is still your best tool, but a fed Yone out-DPSes your lifesteal. Play for splitpush, where his Spirit Cleave shield is at its smallest.

edits.after: Wither is your panic button, and it does more than slow him: Spirit Cleave's cooldown and cast time both scale with attack speed, so cutting it stretches them.

notes: Best find here is that Spirit Cleave's cooldown and cast time scale with attack speed, which turns Wither from a generic slow into a direct cooldown-extension on Yone's shield — nothing in either layer said this. The existing text pointed at the right button (Wither on his engage) via two wrong mechanisms: that Wither interrupts a dash mid-animation, and that it makes a self-centred cone whiff. Neither is true. Also added the Way of the Hunter damage split, which matters because the recommended build in report[8].t is armour-heavy and only answers every second auto. I left the 'let your team body-block his R' line alone — Fate Sealed blinks behind the LAST champion in the line, so whether body-blocking helps or hurts is not something I can settle from the kit file, and I did not want to guess.
